question: Which of the following compounds undergoes thermal decomposition to produce calcium oxide and carbon dioxide?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Calcium Carbonate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Calcium carbonate (CaCO₃)** decomposes upon heating to produce calcium oxide (CaO) and carbon dioxide (CO₂).
 
• The thermal decomposition reaction of calcium carbonate is: CaCO₃ (s) → CaO (s) + CO₂ (g).
 
• This decomposition occurs at a temperature of about 825°C (1517°F).
 
• Calcium oxide (CaO), also known as quicklime, is widely used in construction and industrial processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thermal Decomposition:**

 
 
• It is a chemical reaction where a compound breaks down into simpler compounds or elements upon heating.
 
• Thermal decomposition reactions are usually endothermic, meaning they absorb heat.
 
 
 
• **Calcium Oxide (CaO):**
 
 
• Also known as quicklime or burnt lime.
 
• Used in the manufacture of cement, steel, and paper, and in water treatment.
 
 
 
• **Carbon Dioxide (CO₂):**
 
 
• A colorless, odorless gas that is a byproduct of the respiration of living organisms and the combustion of fossil fuels.
 
• It is used in the production of carbonated beverages, as a refrigerant, and in fire extinguishers.
 
 
 
• **Other Thermal Decomposition Examples:**
 
 
• Calcium nitrate (Ca(NO₃)₂) decomposes to calcium oxide (CaO), nitrogen dioxide (NO₂), and oxygen (O₂).
 
• Calcium sulfate (CaSO₄) decomposes to calcium oxide (CaO) and sulfur trioxide (SO₃).
